title: Making a product line worth displaying
target: How to choose and place a display in Supermarket Simulator so a product line reads as a line rather than as stock left on a shelf.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A product line you want to push

steps.do: Decide the display before you decide the stock, because the display is the game's own object.
steps.because: displays have a manager, data, subtypes and a definition of their own (DisplayManager, DisplayData, DisplaySubType, DisplaySO)

steps.do: Take the colour from the game's set rather than inventing one.
steps.because: the colour side has data of its own and a manager of its own (DisplayColorSO, DisplayColorManager)

steps.do: Match the product to a display type rather than assuming every product belongs on one.
steps.because: products carry a display type of their own (ProductDisplayType)

steps.do: Remember that a product's identity belongs to the product, not to the shelf.
steps.because: each product keeps its own identifier, independent of any shelf (ProductId)

steps.do: Unload crates knowing they carry their contents with them.
steps.because: crates carry product data of their own (CrateProductsData)

steps.do: Let the layout setting decide where things sit.
steps.because: where products sit is decided by a layout setting of its own, and a calculator works out the transform of a displayed product (ProductLayoutConfig, DisplayProductTransformCalculator)

steps.do: Expect the picture on the pack to be handled by the game, not by the model.
steps.because: there is a manager for product pictures, and a product has a renderable form and a kind of material of its own (ProductAtlasManager, ProductRenderable, ProductMaterialType)

steps.do: Count the line in pairs rather than in ones.
steps.because: products are counted as a pair of amounts (ProductCountPair)

commonMistakes: Filling a display with whatever is nearby instead of with a line.
Recolouring by eye when the game has its own colour data for displays.
Treating every product as displayable in the same place.
Moving stock out of a crate without noticing what the crate was carrying.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
